question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}$. Solve $AX = B$ for $X$ using the matrix method. Analyze each intermediate step, including finding $|A|$, computing the adjoint, and interpreting the solution.
explanation:
First, $A = \begin{bmatrix}1&2&1\\0&1&-1\\2&3&4\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\\5\end{bmatrix}$

1. $|A|=1\begin{vmatrix}1&-1\\3&4\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}0&-1\\2&4\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}0&1\\2&3\end{vmatrix}$
$=1(1\cdot4-(-1)\cdot3)-2(0\cdot4-(-1)\cdot2)+1(0\cdot3-1\cdot2)$
$=1(4+3)-2(0+2)+1(0-2)$
$=1(7)-2(2)-2$
$=7-4-2=1$
So $|A|=1$ (non-singular).

2. Find cofactors:
Row 1:
$A_{11}=\begin{vmatrix}1&-1\\3&4\end{vmatrix}=1\cdot4-(-1)\cdot3=4+3=7$
$A_{12}=-\begin{vmatrix}0&-1\\2&4\end{vmatrix}=-(0\cdot4-(-1)\cdot2)=-(0+2)=-2$
$A_{13}=\begin{vmatrix}0&1\\2&3\end{vmatrix}=0\cdot3-1\cdot2=0-2=-2$
Row 2:
$A_{21}=-\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\3&4\end{vmatrix}=-(2\cdot4-1\cdot3)=-(8-3)=-5$
$A_{22}=\begin{vmatrix}1&1\\2&4\end{vmatrix}=1\cdot4-1\cdot2=4-2=2$
$A_{23}=-\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\2&3\end{vmatrix}=-(1\cdot3-2\cdot2)=-(3-4)=1$
Row 3:
$A_{31}=\begin{vmatrix}2&1\\1&-1\end{vmatrix}=2\cdot(-1)-1\cdot1=-2-1=-3$
$A_{32}=-\begin{vmatrix}1&1\\0&-1\end{vmatrix}=-(1\cdot(-1)-1\cdot0)=-(−1−0)=1$
$A_{33}=\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{vmatrix}=1\cdot1-2\cdot0=1-0=1$

Cofactor matrix: $\begin{bmatrix}7&-2&-2\\-5&2&1\\-3&1&1\end{bmatrix}$
Adjoint (transpose): $\begin{bmatrix}7&-5&-3\\-2&2&1\\-2&1&1\end{bmatrix}$

3. $A^{-1}=\operatorname{adj}A/|A|=\operatorname{adj}A$

4. $X=A^{-1}B=\begin{bmatrix}7&-5&-3\\-2&2&1\\-2&1&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2\\-1\\5\end{bmatrix}$

First row: $7\cdot2 -5\cdot(-1) -3\cdot5 = 14+5-15=4$
Second: $-2\cdot2 + 2\cdot(-1) + 1\cdot5 = -4-2+5=-1$
Third: $-2\cdot2 + 1\cdot(-1) + 1\cdot5 = -4-1+5=0$

$X=\begin{bmatrix}4\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}$

So $x=4, y=-1, z=0$.
All intermediate calculations are used in constructing the solution.

options.A: $X=\begin{bmatrix}1\\4\\-1\end{bmatrix}$; since $|A|=0$, the system has infinitely many solutions.
options.B: $X=\begin{bmatrix}4\\0\\-1\end{bmatrix}$; since $|A|=1$, the system has a unique solution.
options.C: $X=\begin{bmatrix}4\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}$; since $|A|=1\ne0$, the system has a unique solution.
options.D: $X=\begin{bmatrix}-4\\1\\0\end{bmatrix}$; since $|A|=-1$, the system has no solution.
